'''David T. Hon''' (born 1941) is a [[Guangdong]]-born<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet the Founder |url=https://usa.dahon.com/pages/meet-the-founder |access-date=2024-11-22 |website=Dahon North America |language=en}}</ref> Taiwanese physicist, inventor and entrepreneur. He is best known as the inventor and founder of [[Dahon]] [[folding bicycle]]s. Dahon has since grown to become the world's largest manufacturer and marketer of folding bikes<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/06_24/b3988102.htm |title=A Commuter's Secret Weapon |work=[[BusinessWeek]] |date=2006-06-12 |accessdate=2012-04-01 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090517095942/http://www.businessweek.com/magazine/content/06_24/b3988102.htm |archivedate=2009-05-17 }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,1587270-2,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070212035102/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0%2C9171%2C1587270-2%2C00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 12, 2007 |title=Trends: Know When to Fold 'Em |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date=2007-02-08 |accessdate=2012-04-20}}</ref> with Hon still CEO to this day.
[[File:Dr. David T. Hon receives an award for contribution to the bicycle industry.jpg|thumb|Dr. David T. Hon, founder and CEO of [[Dahon]], receives and award from Jack Oortwijn, editor in chief of ''Bike Europe'']]

==Early life==
Born 1941, Hon hails from a poor family from [[Hong Kong]]. From the age of 13 through to 18 he worked part-time as an illustrator for his parents' clothing workshop.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bike-eu.com/products/anniversary-campaign-dahon-5840.html |title=Anniversary Campaign Dahon |publisher=Bike Europe |date=2012-05-29 |accessdate=2012-06-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120628001434/http://www.bike-eu.com/products/anniversary-campaign-dahon-5840.html |archivedate=2012-06-28 }}</ref> He received a scholarship to attend, and graduated from, the prestigious Anglican-run [[Diocesan Boys' School]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://newsgroups.derkeiler.com/Archive/Soc/soc.culture.china/2006-02/msg00314.html |title=If anything the problem is worse than in Taiwan |publisher=South China Morning Post Publishers Ltd. |date=2006-02-06 |accessdate=2012-06-12 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304202136/http://newsgroups.derkeiler.com/Archive/Soc/soc.culture.china/2006-02/msg00314.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> in 1959 and the family moved to the U.S. soon afterwards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dahon.com/mainnav/about-dahon-folding-bikes/david-hon.html| title=Dahon Corporate Website|accessdate=2013-06-10}}</ref>

Hon graduated from [[University of California, Berkeley|UC, Berkeley]] in 1964, with a BA in physics and at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]'s physics department, obtained the highest score in the Ph.D. candidacy exam in 1967. Whilst still a doctoral candidate he taught as assistant professor of physics at [[California Polytechnic State University|Cal Poly State U]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bike-eu.com/shows-events/nieuws/2007/8/25-years-dahon-celebrations-1011049 |title=25 years Dahon celebrations |publisher=Bike Europe |date=2007-08-22 |accessdate=2012-06-12 }}</ref> in San Luis Obispo, and, later, as Sr. Lecturer at [[University of Southern California|USC]]. He went on to complete his [[thesis]] as an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] and [[NASA]] scholar at USC where he received his Ph.D. in physics in 1971.

==Career ==
Hon's career in physics truly started when he took up employment at [[Hughes Aircraft]] Company, [[Los Angeles]], one of the world's leading [[aerospace]] corporations. His work focused in particular on the research and development of tactical [[lasers]]. In his early years he became known for his work on high power laser frequency doubling, quickly becoming section head and senior physicist. He became a coauthor in the internationally used ''Laser Handbook'' (North Holland Press, 1979).<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Laser-Handbook-v-M-L-Stitch/dp/toc/0444852719 |title=''Laser Handbook v.3'' M.L. Stitch, North Holland Press, 1979 |publisher=Amazon.co.uk |date=2011-01-02 |accessdate=2012-04-01}}</ref>

In 1977 Hon was drafted into the highly regarded [[HRL Laboratories|Hughes Research Labs]] in [[Malibu, California|Malibu]]. With greater freedom in research choices, this facility is where he began to focus on the pursuit of lasers for [[nuclear fusion]]. By 1980 he had discovered and published a novel technique to efficiently compress high-power laser pulses (to attain over ten times the peak powers) by using Stimulated [[Brillouin scattering#Stimulated Brillouin scattering|Brillouin Scattering]] (SBS) from a tapered [[optical fiber]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=''Optics Letters'' Pulse compression by stimulated Brillouin scattering, 5, 516-518, 1980 |journal=Optics Letters |volume=5 |issue=12 |pages=516–518 |doi=10.1364/OL.5.000516 |pmid=19701291 |publisher=Opticsinfobase.org |date=1980-12-01 |last1=Hon |first1=David T. }}</ref> This work has since inspired hundreds of related research projects right up to the present day.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Uqun_jvJCR8C&q=d.t.+hon+laser&pg=PA223 |title=''Phase Conjugate Laser Optics'', Brignon and Huignard, 2004 |accessdate=2012-04-01|isbn=9780471439578|year=2004|last1=Brignon |first1=Arnaud |last2=Huignard |first2=Jean-Pierre }}</ref> The technique is now widespread in laser nuclear fusion, and ground or space-born defense lasers, as well as in other areas of science and engineering where high, peak-power or high quality laser beams are desired. == Inventor and entrepreneur ==
The [[1973 oil crisis|oil crisis]] of the 1970s coincided with a gradual realization for Hon that for many technical reasons, laser nuclear fusion as the ultimate clean energy solution might never be achieved in his lifetime. For some years already he had been researching the idea of a truly effective [[folding bicycle]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4067589 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120723231817/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4067589 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-23 |title=USPO listing, Foldable Bicycle, 1976 |publisher=Patft.uspto.gov |access-date=2012-04-05 }}</ref> So in 1981 he parted ways with Hughes Research Labs and became a self-employed entrepreneur for practicable [[Environmentally friendly|green]] solutions.

[[File:1982 Hon Convertible folding bicycle.JPG|thumb|Original 1982 Hon Convertible]]
Hon's [[folding bicycle]] was the result of some seven years of garage research and invention.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4448435 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714145133/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4448435 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-14 |title=USPO listing, Foldable and Portable Vehicle, 1982 |publisher=Patft.uspto.gov |access-date=2012-04-05 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4566713 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716140159/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/4566713 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-16 |title=USPO listing, Folding bicycle with releasable brace assembly, 1983 |publisher=Patft.uspto.gov |access-date=2012-04-05 }}</ref> When he was satisfied with the end product, he at first steered towards licensing his folding bike to existing big brands. They however, failed to share in his enthusiasm.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.livestrong.com/article/352370-the-history-of-dahon-bicycles/ |title=''Livestrong.com'', The History of Dahon Bicycles, 2011-01-08 |date= |access-date=2012-04-06}}</ref> With faith undimmed, Hon and his brother Henry raised US$2 million from 35 investors through extensive media exposure and founded [[Dahon]] North America in 1982 (originally Hon California, Inc).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.manta.com/c/mmjn232/dahon-inc |title='Manta', Dahon Inc |date= |access-date=2012-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/05/26/garden/a-commuter-s-solution-bicycle-that-folds-up.html# |title=A Commuter's Solution: Bicycle That Folds Up |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=1988-05-26 |access-date=2012-04-10}}</ref>

Soon after founding the company, Hon decided that to make it more cost effective he would open a factory in [[Taiwan]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qq6GBPoHQpAC&q=hon+folding&pg=PA59 |title=Two Folding Bikes - Easy to Pack, Easy to Pedal |publisher=Popular Science |date=1983-04-01 |access-date=2012-04-20}}</ref> He practically moved to the emerging bicycle industry hot-spot to look after operations, while Henry Hon stayed looking after marketing in the U.S. The business took off, in 1985 alone selling over 10,000 bicycles and by 1994 more than 100,000 annually with 60% of the market share.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://taiwantoday.tw/ct.asp?xItem=99363&CtNode=124 |title=''Taiwan Today'', A Bicycle Built for Profits |date=1994-01-03 |access-date=2012-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233406/http://taiwantoday.tw/ct.asp?xItem=99363&CtNode=124 |archive-date=2016-03-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Dahon continued to grow in popularity worldwide among commuters, vacationers and cyclists.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bikeradar.com/news/article/dahon-sales-rise-as-commuting-takes-center-stage-22844/ |title=Dahon sales rise as commuting takes center stage |date=2009-08-19 |access-date=2012-04-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bike-eu.com/news/dahon-again-record-breaking-despite-financial-crisis-3109.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120719114459/http://www.bike-eu.com/news/dahon-again-record-breaking-despite-financial-crisis-3109.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-19 |title=Dahon Again Record Breaking despite Financial Crisis |publisher=Bike Europe |date=2008-11-19 |access-date=2012-04-20 }}</ref>

|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120711155633/http://exhibition.ifdesign.de/winner_en.html?ma_id=5919 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-11 |title=Dahon:Portrait&Awards |publisher=iF Online Exhibition |access-date=2012-04-10 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biketaiwan.com/eNews.asp?issue=19#Product%20News_1 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721143417/http://www.biketaiwan.com/eNews.asp?issue=19%23Product%20News_1 |url-status=dead|title=Product of The Year-Dahon Flo Folding Bike |publisher=Taiwan Bicycle Source |date=2005-04-20 |access-date=2012-04-20 |archive-date = 2012-07-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.totalbike.com/web/articles/ta9.html |title=Dahon: Presto  |publisher=Total Bike |access-date=2012-04-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mail.mcvuk.com/news/read/dahon-bags-two-taipei-awards/07463 |title=Dahon bags two Taipei awards |publisher=Bike Biz |date=2009-04-14 |access-date=2012-06-13 }}{{dead link|date=December 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and has registered 220+ patents related to foldable bikes,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://appft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&d=PG01&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/srchnum.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&s1=20040190984.PGNR. |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707040424/http://appft1.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&d=PG01&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/srchnum.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&s1=20040190984.PGNR. |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-07 |title=USPO listing, Inner-lock foldable joint, 2003 |publisher=Patft.uspto.gov |access-date=2012-04-05 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/5269550 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120712145044/http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect2=PTO1&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&d=PALL&RefSrch=yes&Query=PN/5269550 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2012-07-12 |title=USPO listing, Mountain bike, 1991 |publisher=Patft.uspto.gov |access-date=2012-04-05 }}</ref> many in Asia where most bikes are produced. A few of these innovations/inventions have become standard features in nearly all folding bikes today.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bike-eu.com/news/dahon-inks-patent-license-agreement-with-nationalpanasonic-133.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118103244/http://www.bike-eu.com/news/dahon-inks-patent-license-agreement-with-nationalpanasonic-133.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-01-18 |title=Dahon Inks Patent License Agreement with National/Panasonic |publisher=Bike Europe |date=2000-02-10 |access-date=2012-06-13 }}</ref> Hon's inventions have been widely copied, both legally and illegally and he has become quite involved in [[Intellectual property|IP]] protection advocacy. He is currently chairman of the Industrial Intellectual Property Committee of the Shenzhen Federation of Industrial Economics, has assisted in pushing through legislation that protects foreign companies operating in China and has been published on the subject in China's largest economic journal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bicycleretailer.com/news/newsDetail/6186.html |title=Brands Push to Stem Flow of Fake Product |publisher=Bicycle Retailer |date=2011-11-18 |access-date=2012-04-08}}</ref>

In 1995 Dahon opened its [[ISO 9000#Contents of ISO 9001|ISO 9001]] certified<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cyclemotion.co.uk/dahon/dahonnews9.htm |title=''Cycle Motion'', Dahon's Shenzhen, China Factory Awarded ISO 9001 Certification, 2002 |publisher=Cyclemotion.co.uk |date=2002-11-29 |access-date=2012-04-01}}</ref> factory in [[Shenzhen]], China. The company has since grown to officially become the world's largest producer of folding bikes,<ref>Guinness World Records 2000 Millennium Edition, 2000, p. 301</ref> turning out about half a million units a year<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bikeradar.com/news/article/dahon-to-move-some-bike-production-to-europe-30530/ |title=''Bike Radar'', Dahon to move some bike production to Europe, 2011 |publisher=Bikeradar.com |date=2011-06-10 |access-date=2012-04-01}}</ref> with over 5 million bikes sold to date, mostly under its own brands. Dahon today operates seven factories or subsidiaries in three continents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bicyclenewswire.com/index.cfm?fuseaction=home.showreleasemore&id=3038 |title=''Bicycle News Wire'', Dahon Enhances Global Manufacturing, Adds Key Management, 2011 |publisher=Bicyclenewswire.com |access-date=2012-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120424225209/http://www.bicyclenewswire.com/index.cfm?fuseaction=home.showreleasemore&id=3038 |archive-date=2012-04-24 |url-status=usurped }}</ref> Hon remains CEO while still contributing inventions and designs.

In 2013, Dr. David Hon was furthermore nominated for UC Berkeley Excellence in Achievement Award for his "contributions in high-powered lasers as well as his role in revolutionizing the modern-day folding bicycle."

{{blockquote|In the last decades we have seen first-hand the varied ways that portable bikes can contribute to a greener and better way of life&nbsp;... City governments and transport authorities have eased regulations and opened new opportunities for commuters to use bikes as an intermodal means of personal mobility. These are very promising first steps into an even more widespread rethinking of transportation in the next few years.|Dr. David T. Hon, 2009,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bike-eu.com/news/david-hon-speaker-at-velo-city-3411.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130118055048/http://www.bike-eu.com/news/david-hon-speaker-at-velo-city-3411.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-01-18 |title=David Hon Speaker at Velo-city |publisher=Bikeradar.com |date=2009-05-11 |access-date=2012-04-20 }}</ref>}}

==Personal life==
Hon is married to Florence Shen, has sons Joshua and Reuel (an associate director at MGM who has since died) and grand children. He has four younger brothers Peter, Richard, Paul (a Christian missionary), and Henry.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dahonbikes.com/index.php?id=49 |title=''Dahon Corporate Website'' |access-date=2012-04-06}}</ref>

Hon is interested in the arts and anthropology. He is good at painting, musical instruments like piano, and ballroom dancing. Hon plays basketball and ping-pong regularly, and is fluent in English, Mandarin and Cantonese.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bicyclingaustralia.com.au/content/2010/bicycling-australia-2008-jul-aug/inside-china |title=Inside China |publisher=Bicycling Australia |date=July 2008 |access-date=2012-06-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328085636/http://bicyclingaustralia.com.au/content/2010/bicycling-australia-2008-jul-aug/inside-china |archive-date=2012-03-28 }}</ref>
